findings.title: A single NaN in continuous hue silently collapses the entire color mapping to 2 colors
findings.repro:
import os; os.environ['MPLBACKEND']='Agg'
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt, hypertools as hyp
d = np.random.default_rng(1).standard_normal((60, 4)).cumsum(axis=0)
hue = np.arange(60.0); hue[7] = np.nan
fig = hyp.plot(d, fmt='.', hue=hue, ndims=2, palette='viridis')
fig.canvas.draw()
fc = np.vstack([c.get_facecolors() for c in fig.axes[0].collections])
print(np.unique(np.round(fc, 5), axis=0).shape[0])  # -> 2 (60 without the NaN)
findings.expected: Either an informative ValueError/warning about NaN in hue, or NaN-aware binning (nanmin/nanmax edges + sentinel color) so the 59 valid values keep their 60-color gradient.
findings.actual:
palette=viridis: unique colors clean=60  with-1-NaN=2
   COLLAPSED example colors: [[0.27, 0.015, 0.341, 1.0], [0.974, 0.904, 0.13, 1.0]]
palette=hls: unique colors clean=60  with-1-NaN=2  (no warning, no error)

findings.title: morph_samples=-5 leaks a numpy internal error ('negative dimensions are not allowed')
findings.repro:
import os; os.environ['MPLBACKEND']='Agg'
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
hyp.plot([rng.standard_normal((60, 4)), rng.standard_normal((60, 4))], animate='morph', morph_samples=-5, duration=2, frame_rate=10)
findings.expected: ValueError: morph_samples= must be a positive int (or None); got -5.
findings.actual: ValueError: negative dimensions are not allowed

findings.title: legend= list length mismatch error names 'label=' instead of the kwarg the user passed
findings.repro:
import os; os.environ['MPLBACKEND']='Agg'
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
hyp.plot([rng.standard_normal((40, 4)) for _ in range(3)], fmt='.', legend=['A', 'B'])
findings.expected: Error text mentioning legend= (the kwarg actually supplied).
findings.actual: ValueError: label= was given as a list/tuple of length 2, but there are 3 dataset(s) to plot; pass either a single value (broadcast to every dataset) or a list/tuple of length 3.
